{"metadata":{"description":"Expose a running DeepSeek Harness as an MCP server, so Claude Code, Codex or any MCP client can drive its workspaces, sessions, files, shell and agent tools, and read token usage and cost receipts.","id":"gh:1397276265","install_available":true,"language":"TypeScript","name":"dsh-as-mcp","slug":"xiseliuli/dsh-as-mcp","topics":["cordis-plugin","deepseek-harness","dsh","dsh-plugin","mcp","model-context-protocol"]},"paragraphs":[{"id":"p1s1","text":"Expose a running DeepSeek Harness as an MCP server, so Claude Code, Codex or any MCP client can driv"},{"id":"p1s2","text":"e its workspaces, sessions, files, shell and agent tools, and read token usage and cost receipts."},{"id":"p2s1","text":"English | 中文"},{"id":"p3s1","text":"Expose a running **DeepSeek Harness** as an **MCP server**, so any other agent — Claude
Code, Codex,"},{"id":"p3s2","text":" another DSH, a CI job, your own script — can drive it: create workspaces,
start sessions, hand the "},{"id":"p3s3","text":"DSH agent a coding task, read and write files, run commands."},{"id":"p4s1","text":"The endpoint runs *inside* the DSH host process, so a session created over MCP is a real
DSH session"},{"id":"p4s2","text":". It appears live in the DSH UI, runs inside the DSH sandbox, and is subject to
the same permission "},{"id":"p4s3","text":"policy as anything you type yourself. Nothing about the agent is
reimplemented."},{"id":"p5s1","text":"## Security"},{"id":"p6s1","text":"This endpoint is remote control of a coding agent that has shell access. Treat the token like
an SSH"},{"id":"p6s2","text":" key — and note that the plugin does too: no tool returns its value. `dsh_info` reports
where the to"},{"id":"p6s3","text":"ken comes from (a file path or the composition), never the literal, so a calling
agent's transcript "},{"id":"p6s4","text":"never accumulates the credential. A pinned token shorter than 16 characters
draws a warning at boot,"},{"id":"p6s5","text":" and a generated one is 43 characters of CSPRNG output."},{"id":"p7s1","text":"- A request that declares a body over 64 MiB is refused with `413` before the body
is read, and a ch"},{"id":"p7s2","text":"unked request — which declares no size — has its bytes counted while
streaming and is refused with t"},{"id":"p7s3","text":"he same `413` once the cap is passed (verified: 70 MB
sent chunked answered `413` in 71 ms, and a va"},{"id":"p7s4","text":"lid chunked request still works). This
is defence in depth: every tool that could carry a large payl"},{"id":"p7s5","text":"oad already has its own
cap.
- A rejected request answers `401` with `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer realm"},{"id":"p7s6","text":"="dsh-as-mcp"`, so a standard
MCP client can tell that presenting its configured token is the fix ra"},{"id":"p7s7","text":"ther than reporting a dead
endpoint. The realm is a fixed label; the token is never echoed.
- The li"},{"id":"p7s8","text":"stener binds to `127.0.0.1` and every request is bearer-checked, including requests on
a route mount"},{"id":"p7s9","text":"ed on DSH's own web server. That check is the *only* gate there: an exact route
registered on the we"},{"id":"p7s10","text":"b server is matched **before** DSH's authorization fence — anything
unmatched is handed to that fenc"},{"id":"p7s11","text":"e as a fallback (`webserver/src/index.ts:222-227`) — so with
`http.mountOnWebServer: true` the endpo"},{"id":"p7s12","text":"int does not inherit your browser session's
protection, it enforces its own. One caveat on DSH Deskt"},{"id":"p7s13","text":"op: when ordinary browser access is
disabled there, the web server additionally refuses requests tha"},{"id":"p7s14","text":"t do not carry the renderer
header, so the mounted path is unreachable for a plain MCP client — use "},{"id":"p7s15","text":"the plugin-owned
listener. Setting `http.host: 0.0.0.0` exposes that same power to your network; the"},{"id":"p7s16","text":" plugin
warns at bind time, and you should do it only behind your own gateway.
- **The token is the "},{"id":"p7s17","text":"entire security boundary, and that boundary is your user account.** There

`dsh_"},{"id":"p9s2","text":"info.toolAvailability` derives the same mapping at runtime for the caller's own profile, but an
oper"},{"id":"p9s3","text":"ator setting up a profile should be able to read the requirements in one place. "Required" means
the"},{"id":"p9s4","text":" tool does not work at all without it; "configured" means the service is present in normal profiles
"},{"id":"p9s5","text":"but a deployment can switch the capability off."},{"id":"p10s1","text":"| Tool group | Requires | Notes |"},{"id":"p11s1","text":"| `dsh_info`, `session_usage` (by id) | nothing beyond the durable log | `session_usage` by id works"},{"id":"p11s2","text":" as long as the log is readable (`sessionQuery`, or the controller's `inspect` fallback) |
| `sessio"},{"id":"p11s3","text":"n_create` / `session_list` / `session_prompt` / `session_messages` / `session_cancel` / `session_for"},{"id":"p11s4","text":"k` / `session_rename` / `session_set_model` | `sessionController` | the bridge waits for it only whe"},{"id":"p11s5","text":"re it must (`session_create`/`prompt`); elsewhere the tool reports the missing service |
| `session_"},{"id":"p11s6","text":"search` | `sessionController.search` **and** a session-query index that is open | `session-query-sql"},{"id":"p11s7","text":"ite` ships with `openAt: "never"`; set it to `startup` or `first-search` to enable search |
| `works"},{"id":"p11s8","text":"pace_*` | `workspaceRegistry` | provided by the base bundle in normal profiles |
| `file_*` | `fs` |"},{"id":"p11s9","text":" the deployment's sandbox policy still applies; `file_read_image` additionally needs a supported ima"},{"id":"p11s10","text":"ge format |
| `shell_*` | `shell` | `shell_run` uses `run()` when present and `execute()` otherwise;"},{"id":"p11s11","text":" background jobs need `start()` or `execute()` |
| `dsh_tool_list` / `dsh_tool_call` | `tools` **and"},{"id":"p11s12","text":"** `sessionController.resolveAgent` | the allow-list is applied on top of the session's own policy |"},{"id":"p11s13","text":"
| money in usage replies | `costMeter` | a third-party price plugin (`dsh-cost-meter`); absent by d"},{"id":"p11s14","text":"efault, and the reply says so |
| `approval.policy: "allow"` | `approval` **and** a resolvable agent"},{"id":"p11s15","text":" | absent service or agent means the create/fork reply reports `approvalPolicyError` |
| `http.mount"},{"id":"p11s16","text":"OnWebServer` | `webServer` | the plugin waits for it and mounts; `dsh_info.mountNote` says while it "},{"id":"p11s17","text":"bServer` | the plugin waits for it and mounts; `dsh_info.mountNote` says while it is still waiting |"},{"id":"p12s1","text":"## Compatibility"},{"id":"p13s1","text":"- **Harness** ≥ `0.1.5-rc.1`, declared as `peerDependencies["@deepseek-ai/dsh"]:
">=0.1.5-rc.1"` wit"},{"id":"p13s2","text":"h no upper bound. DSH's plugin loader reads that range straight from the
manifest and semver-checks "},{"id":"p13s3","text":"it against the single running runtime version (prereleases
included) *before* the plugin is imported"},{"id":"p13s4","text":"; an incompatible install is refused unless the host
grants an exact-version exemption (`dsh plugin "},{"id":"p13s5","text":"allow-version`).
- **Node** `^22.19.0 || >=24.0.0`.
- The `@deepseek-ai/dsh` peer is declared **opti"},{"id":"p13s6","text":"onal**, purely so `dsh plugin add` does not pull
a full harness install into every profile just to s"},{"id":"p13s7","text":"atisfy it. Optional only changes
installation — DSH's compatibility gate reads `peerDependencies` re"},{"id":"p13s8","text":"gardless of
`peerDependenciesMeta`, so the version check above still applies in full.
- **Settings m"},{"id":"p13s9","text":"odel.** Verified against `dsh 0.2.0-rc.2`, whose settings service replaced the
0.1.x API this plugin"},{"id":"p13s10","text":" first shipped against: `settings.installSection` is gone, a namespace is
projected from the entry's"},{"id":"p13s11","text":" own `Config` keyed by the Loader row id, and only `meta.volatile`
fields are editable — a volatile "},{"id":"p13s12","text":"write is committed into the running reference without a
remount. The host half therefore declares no"},{"id":"p13s13","text":" registration at all and reads its configuration
through `plainConfig()` on every access, and the on"},{"id":"p13s14","text":"ly settings call it still makes is
`configure({ auto: false }, ctx.fiber)` (it ships its own page). "},{"id":"p13s15","text":"**The panel needs the 0.2
